:::{#thm-weibull-mean}
#### Weibull mean

If $T$ has the Weibull distribution with shape $\shape$ and rate $\rate$, then:

$$\E{T} = \gammafn(1+1/\shape)\cdot \rate^{-1/\shape}$$

:::

::: proof

For the mean, use the [survival-function formula for the mean](expectation.qmd#thm-surv-mean)
and substitute $u = \rate t^\shape$,
so that $t = (u/\rate)^{1/\shape}$ and $dt = \frac{1}{\shape}\rate^{-1/\shape} u^{1/\shape - 1}\,du$:

$$
\ba
\E{T}
&= \int_0^\infty \text{e}^{-\rate t^\shape}\,dt
&& (\text{expectation via the survival function}) \\
&= \frac{1}{\shape}\rate^{-1/\shape} \int_0^\infty u^{1/\shape - 1} \text{e}^{-u}\,du
&& (\text{substitute } u = \rate t^\shape) \\
&= \frac{1}{\shape}\rate^{-1/\shape}\,\gammafn(1/\shape)
&& (\text{definition of the gamma function}) \\
&= \gammafn(1 + 1/\shape)\,\rate^{-1/\shape}
&& (\gammafn(1 + a) = a\,\gammafn(a))
\ea
$$

:::
